content.value: This SARIT edition is based on Nanda Kishore Sharma’s 1932 edition. I (Andrew Ollett) ran it through Google Cloud Vision OCR, then automatically transliterated the output, and removed the layers of commentary and notes. I added some structure and corrected mistakes when I spotted them. Surely some mistakes will remain.

children.translated_text: First Canto (<s>Ucchvāsa</s>)

children.text: jayati girisutāyāḥ kāmasaṁtāpavāhinyurasi rasaniṣē kaścāndanaścandra mauliḥ
children.translated_text: Victorious is a certain <s>Candra</s>-crested one [<s>Śiva</s>], who is sandal-paste upon the breast of the daughter of the mountain [<s>Pārvatī</s>], quenching the burning fever of desire,

children.text: tadanu ca vijayantē kīrtibhājāṁ kavīnāmasadamr̥tabindusyandinō vāgvilāsāḥ
children.translated_text: And thereafter victorious are the verbal sports of fame-possessing poets, dripping drops of immortal nectar,
Victorious is a certain <s>Kandarpa</s> (god of love), who has spring as his companion, who is the aged root of the vine of the entire cycle of existence, giving rise to birth,

children.text: tadanu punar apāṅgōtsaṅgasaṁcāritānāṁ jayati taruṇayōṣillōcanānāṁ vilāsaḥ
children.translated_text: And thereafter victorious is the sport of the eyes of young women, set in motion in the corner-glances,
Unfathomably deep in its inner vibration, a temple of divine bliss,
I praise the stream of <s>Sarasvatī</s> [eloquence], flowing, mature with various <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments),
Clear, stealing beauty, skilled in various kinds of <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) —

children.text: bhavanti kasyacit puṇyair mukhē vācō gr̥hē striyaḥ
children.translated_text: by someone's merit, such words grace the mouth, and such women grace the home,

children.text: kiṁ kavēs tēna kāvyēna kiṁ kāṇḍēna dhanuṣmataḥ
children.translated_text: What use is that poem to a poet, what use is that arrow to an archer,

children.text: parasya hr̥dayē lagnaṁ na ghūrṇayati yacchiraḥ
children.translated_text: which, lodged in another's heart, does not make the head reel?
Faltering in their placement of words, causes of maternal affection,
there are some poets of many babbling words, like little children,
Knowing the practice of prayer-bead recitation, seated on <s>kuśa</s>-grass seats,
like <s>Brāhmī</s> [<s>Sarasvatī</s>] herself — the assembly of wicked folk is to be saluted, wearing a girdle,
I salute the company of the wise, a mine of gems of fine verse,
in whose midst even a lowly glass, having fallen, is esteemed as a jewel,

children.text: atrijātasya yā mūrtiḥ śaśinaḥ sajanasya ca
children.translated_text: What comparison is there between the form of the moon, born of <s>Atri</s>, who is among the good,

children.text: kva sā vai rātrijātasya tamasō durjanasya ca
children.translated_text: and darkness, born of night, which belongs among the wicked?

children.text: niścitaṁ sasuraḥ kō ’pi na kulīnaḥ samē ’matiḥ
children.translated_text: Surely, one who is without discernment on an equal ground is not noble, even with a father-in-law,
one who does not delight in poetry that is in every way connected with the divine (<s>asura</s>),
Though possessing faults, yet faultless; though containing sharpness, yet utterly soft —

children.text: namastasmai kr̥tā yēna ramyā rāmāyaṇī kathā
children.translated_text: Salutations to him by whom was composed the delightful tale of <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>,

children.text: vyāsaḥ kṣamābhr̥tāṁ śrēṣṭhō vandyaḥ sa himavāniva
children.translated_text: <s>Vyāsa</s>, the foremost among kings of the earth, is to be venerated like <s>Himavān</s> (the Himalayas),
by whom was created the <s>Bhārata</s>, of vast expanse, beautiful as the gaze of <s>Gaurī</s>,
With eyes like <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>, bewildered by the play of glances reaching the ears,

children.text: karōti kasya nāhādaṁ kathā kāntēva bhāratī
children.translated_text: to whom does the <s>Bhāratī</s> (story of the Bhārata), like a beloved woman, not bring delight?
By him who eternally has eloquence as his companion, who bears the form of a bow (<s>namad-ākāra</s>),
who is rich in virtues like a bow [with its string], all people have been delighted,
Thus, through the narration of poetic tales by these poets,
the wise, with ears and hearts filled to the brim, like vessels with water,
The words of those like us, whose intellect falters in discerning what is proper to say —

children.text: lapsyantē kva kilāvakāśam athavā sarvasahāḥ sūrayaḥ
children.translated_text: where indeed will they find scope? But then, the learned are all-enduring,
Words may become harsh due to the particular use of puns and <s>śleṣa</s> (double meanings),

children.text: nōdvēgas tatra kartavyō yasmān naikō ēsaḥ kavēḥ
children.translated_text: one should not take offense at that, for this is not the only [way] of a poet,
Of a poem, as of a mango fruit — whether soft or of the other kind —
the <s>rasa</s> (flavor/aesthetic sentiment) itself becomes different through the particular shade of composition,
of <s>Vidhī</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), who descended into the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s> compelled by his all-pervading activity, expert in the seasonal rituals —
the lineage of the great sage named <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>.
There is — of the blessed one whose lotus feet are worshipped by the entire host of sages, humans, and gods,

children.text: śrūyantē ca yatra śravaṇōcitāścandanapallacā iva kēcidanūcānāḥ śucayaḥ

children.translated_text: truth-speaking, radiant with the splendor of <s>Virañci</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), of venerable conduct, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who know <s>Brahman</s>.
And therein are heard certain learned ones, fit for the ear like sandal-paste leaves, pure,

children.text: na ca yē laṅkāpuruṣāḥ, sasūtrāś ca na ca yē lampaṭāḥ, prasiddhāś ca na ca yē lampākāḥ,
children.translated_text: and they are not demons of <s>Laṅkā</s>; and they wear sacred threads, but are not libertines; and they are famous, but not [from] <s>Lampāka</s>,

children.text: kāmavarṣāś ca na ca yē laṅghanāḥ sanmārgasya, navavayasō ’pi na ca yē lambālakāḥ,
children.translated_text: and they shower desires, but do not transgress the righteous path; though of fresh youth, they do not have disheveled locks,

children.text: mahābhāratikāś ca na ca yē raṅgōpajīvinaḥ, sēvitāpsarasō ’pi na ca yē rambhayā
children.translated_text: and they are versed in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, but are not performers on stage; they are attended by <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs), but not accompanied by <s>Rambhā</s>
[specifically].
And [there are] noble people (<s>puṇyajana</s>) —
Why say more —

children.text: jānanti hi guṇāncaktuṁ tadvidhā ēva tādr̥śām
children.translated_text: Indeed, only those of such a kind know how to appreciate the virtues of such persons,
<s>Viśvambharā</s> (the Earth) alone knows the weight of mountains, the abode of greatness,
In their lineage of bright fame, there was born a son of <s>Śrīdhara</s>,
Like a sun, blossoming his own intellect, discerning in Vedic learning,
whose ocean of the nectar of fame, with rising waves, people in every direction
even today drink with greedy eyes through the cups of their ears,
By whose various personal virtues the three worlds were adorned as with a <s>tilaka</s> mark,
from him was I born, a son, a vessel of dullness — <s>Trivikrama</s>,
I, who am foolish, deludedly wish to act like a swan — as a lame man desires [to walk],
Dull-witted, I likewise wish to play the chief among poets,
By me, attempting the difficult task of composing a narrative bound with puns and <s>śleṣa</s> (double meanings),
an ocean, difficult to cross, has been undertaken [to be crossed] with [only] two arms,
Utterances are made easily by the brazen-cheeked foul-mouthed, with inflated cheeks,

children.text: jānāti hi punaḥ samyak kavir ēva kavēḥ śramam
children.translated_text: but only a poet truly knows the labor of a poet,
Accompanied by a caravan of gods, delightful, long sheltered by <s>Meru</s>,
like the garden-garland of <s>Nandana</s> — let this tale be viewed by those at ease,
Possessing an exalted hero, endowed with virtuous meters and <s>muktakas</s> (independent verses),

children.text: campūś ca hārayaṭiś ca kēna na kriyatē hr̥di
children.translated_text: who does not hold dear a <s>campū</s> and a <s>hārayaṭi</s> [type of composition]?

children.text: tathā nākalōkasya, grāmyakavikathāvandha iva nōrasa sya manōharaḥ, bhīma iva
children.translated_text: to the world of heaven, not [merely] pleasing like the narrative compositions of rustic poets but [truly] charming, like <s>Bhīma</s>
an ornament of the <s>Bhārata</s>, like the touch of a beloved's bosom — foremost among all the domains of experience,
like one who has not studied grammar — [yet naturally] exhibiting elision, root-forms, preverbs, augments, and phonetic modifications, like the matted locks of <s>Paśupati</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) —
a tangle in which [are found] blooming golden lotuses and blue lilies, with fluttering pollen dusting the swans,
adorned at its banks by flocks of <s>cakora</s> birds, <s>cakravāka</s> ducks, and <s>kāraṇḍava</s> waterfowl moving abundantly,
with its surging waves forming as it were a stairway-pathway to heaven, [bearing] the victory banner of the king's fame —
flooded with the holy waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, adorned in one part by the <s>Candrabhāgā</s> [river], the essence of the entire wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: śaharāyaḥ purāvakāriṇāma, ārāmō rāmaṇāyakakadalīvanasya, dhāma dharmasya,
children.translated_text: a fortress for the anciently renowned, a garden of the beautiful plantain grove, the abode of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: spadaṁ saṁpadām, āśrayaḥ śrēyasām, ākaraḥ sādhuvyavahāraratnānām, ā
children.translated_text: the seat of prosperity, the refuge of auspiciousness, a mine of gems of righteous conduct,
the academy for the teachings of noble conventions — the land called <s>Āryāvarta</s>.
There is [a land] shining as the ornament of the forehead of the entire expanse of the earth, equal in its worthiness of service
are partakers of all worldly happiness,
Wherein the people, freed from all afflictions by unceasing instruction in righteous deeds, living a full human lifespan,

the doctrine of <s>sphoṭa</s> (linguistic explosion) [is found only] among grammarians, confluence of humors (<s>saṃnipāta</s>) [only] in musical rhythms, planetary transits [only] in the treatises of astronomy,
the theory of elemental modifications [only] among the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>, waning (<s>kṣaya</s>) [only] in lunar days, growth of tumors (<s>gulma</s>) [only] in forest lands, seizure of the throat
[only] in fish, swelling of boils [only] in mountainous forest regions, the binding of colic pain [only] in the temples of <s>Caṇḍikā</s> — [these are] seen
[only there], not among the people.
For instance — the application of ointments (<s>kuṣṭhayoga</s>) [is found only] in the shops of perfumers,

children.text: yatra caturagōpaśōbhitāḥ saṅgrāmā iva grāmāḥ, tujhasakalabhavanāḥ sarvatra
nagā iva nagarapradēśāḥ, sadācaraṇamaṇḍanāni nūpurāṇīva purāṇi, sadāna
children.translated_text: are like mountains; the towns, decorated with perpetual good conduct, are like anklets; the people, always enjoying pleasures,

children.text: bhōgāḥ prabhañjanā iva janāḥ, priyālapanasārāṇi yauvanānīva vanāni, viṭa
children.translated_text: are like storms; the forests, whose essence is the sweet chatter of loved ones, are like the prime of youth;
the gardens, screened by vines, are like maidservants; the sugarcane field enclosures, places of delight, are like good wives;
the reaches of the lakes, of indeterminate waters, are like beast-men of no fixed measure; the wells, stirred up by agitated monkey-troops,

children.text: lākulitā laड़kēśvarakiṁkarā iva bhannakumbhakarṇaṁghanasvāpāḥ kūpāḥ, pīvarō
children.translated_text: like the servants of the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> breaking <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>'s deep slumber, are deep in sleep; the cows, with swollen udders,

children.text: dhasaḥ sarita iva gāvaḥ, saṁtīvratāpadōṣāḥ sūryadvayutaya iva kulastriyaḥ.
children.translated_text: are like rivers; the women of noble families, whose heat of austerity is intense, are like a pair of suns,
Where the villages, adorned with four-fold cattle, are like battlefields; the city-areas, with tall structures in every home,

children.text: yatra ca manōhārisārasadvandvāstatpuruṣēṇa dvigunā cādhiṣṭhitāḥ kādamba

children.translated_text: presided over [by compound-words] and displaying much rice (<s>bahuvrīhi</s> — also a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound),
And where the rice-fields, displaying abundant rice, are like <s>Kādambarī</s> prose compositions — with lovely <s>sārasa</s>-crane pairs, doubled by the [reflected] image (<s>tatpuruṣa</s>),
Why say more —

children.text: nāsti sā nagarī yatra na vāpī na payōdharā
children.translated_text: There is no city where no tank, no cloud [or breast] (<s>payodhara</s>)

children.text: dr̥śyatē na ca yatra strī navāpīnapayōdharā
children.translated_text: is seen — and where there is no woman with fresh, full breasts (<s>nava-apīna-payodhara</s>),
And moreover —
In the month of <s>Phālguna</s>, the branches of trees become devoid of leaves (<s>vipallava</s>),

children.text: jāyantē na tu lōkasya kadāpi ca vipallavāḥ
children.translated_text: but calamities (<s>vipallava</s>) never befall the people,

children.text: nirbharāḥ, satatamakulīnaṁ kulīnāḥ, prāptavimānamaprāpta vimānabhaṅgāḥ, katipaya
children.translated_text: always noble among the noble, having attained celestial chariots (<s>vimāna</s>) yet free from the fall of pride (<s>vimāna-bhaṅga</s>), resplendent with manifold
riches though possessing only a few [worldly] treasures, laugh at the heaven-dwelling folk,
Where the people, their minds delighted by good governance, overflowing with the unbroken succession of great festivals augmented by all prosperity,
And how is that [land] not superior to heaven?

children.text: yatra gr̥hē gr̥hē gauryaḥ striyaḥ, mahēśvarō lōkaḥ, sakṣīkā harayaḥ, padē padē

children.translated_text: there are wealth-givers — [these are] the guardians of the world (<s>Lokapāla</s>s).
Where in every home there are fair women (<s>Gaurī</s>s), the people are great lords (<s>Maheśvara</s>s), the elders are witness-bearing <s>Hari</s>s, at every step
Only <s>Indra</s>, the lord of the gods, is not the king [here],
[among the people].
nor is there any <s>Vināyaka</s> (obstacle-creator)

children.text: yatra calatāsaṁvandhaḥ kalikōpakramaś ca pādapēṣu dr̥śyatē na puruṣēṣu.
children.translated_text: Where the association with creepers and the onset of strife (<s>kali</s>) are seen in trees, not in men.

children.text: yatra camarakavārtā paramahimōpaghātaś ca tuhinācalasthalīṣu śrūyatē na

children.translated_text: among the people.
Where the talk of <s>camara</s>-yaks and the diminution of supreme glory are heard [only] on the snow-mountain plateaus, not

children.text: yaś ca nītimatpuruṣādhiṣṭhitō ’py anītiḥ, saṭō ’py avaṭasaṁkulaḥ, kārūpa

children.translated_text: (<s>kārūpa</s>), is not devoid of beauty of form,
And which [land], though governed by men of policy, is free from injustice (<s>anīti</s>); though possessing thorns (<s>saṭa</s>), is full of pits [only in terrain]; though equipped with artisans

children.text: yatra ca guruvyatikramaṁ nakṣatrarāśayaḥ, mātrākalahaṁ lēkhaśālikāḥ, mitrō

children.translated_text: [these things are done by those creatures],
not by the people.

Where the constellations [perform] transgression against the preceptor (<s>guru</s> = <s>Bṛhaspati</s>), the <s>lekhaśālikā</s> birds [display] quarreling with the mother, the owls [show] hatred at the friend's rise (<s>mitrodaya</s>), the cuckoos [perform] abandonment of offspring, the summer days [cause] destruction of kinsmen (<s>bandhujīva</s> flowers),
Why say more —

children.text: dēśaḥ puṇyatamōddēśaḥ kasyālau na priyō bhavēt
children.translated_text: Who would not find dear this land, the most sacred of regions,
which is joined with leagues (<s>yojana</s>s) as it were with compassionate people?

children.text: tasya viṣayamadhyē niṣadhōṁ nāmāsti janapadaḥ prathitaḥ
children.translated_text: In the midst of that realm, there is a celebrated territory called <s>Niṣadha</s>,
There, worthy of being the abode of the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), is the city called <s>Niṣadhā</s>,
Always gladdened in mind by the policies of its people, made joyful by a perpetually good sovereign,

children.text: sā nagarī nagatanayā gaurīva manōharā bhāti
children.translated_text: that city shines, beautiful like <s>Gaurī</s> (daughter of the mountain), who is the daughter of the mountain,

children.text: rāgragrāsalālasāḥ skhalantaḥ khē khēdayanti madhyēdinaṁ sādinaṁ ravirathatura
children.translated_text: at whose edges the horses of the sun-chariot, stumbling, eager to graze, weary at midday, cause distress to the sun
[himself],
In which, [with palace towers] whose peaks of sapphire-halls touch the clouds, with nets of dense rays serving as the grassy lawn-tips
there fall swarms of innocent bees, mistaking them for tender reddish lotuses
within the clear waters,
In which, upon the crystal and gem-stone-paved courtyard-floors of the houses, where tread the crimson-lac footprint-marks of the moving housewives,

children.text: yāmavalōkayantyaḥ kr̥tāparastrīśaṅkāḥ katham api pratyānīyantē priyaiḥ priyatamāḥ.
children.translated_text: the beloved wives, suspecting another woman, are somehow reassured by their husbands,
In which, upon the bright, transparent walls of residences constructed of various gems, beholding their own reflections,

children.text: yasyāṁ ca divyadēvakulālaṁkr̥tāḥ svargāḥ iva mārgāḥ, satatamapāṁsuvasanāḥ
sāgarā iva nāgarāḥ samantavāraṇāni vanānīva bhavanāti, sura sēnānvitāḥ
children.translated_text: are like oceans; the houses, with elephants tethered all around, are like forests; the wells, accompanied by auspicious troops,

children.text: svargabhūpā iva kūpāḥ, adhikaṁdharōddēśamudbhāsayantō hārā iva vihārāḥ.
children.translated_text: are like kings of heaven; the pleasure-gardens, illuminating the elevated ground, are like necklaces,
In which the streets, adorned with divine temples, are like heavens; the citizens, always wearing spotless garments,

children.text: yasyāṁ ca bahulakṣaṇā sudhāvantō dr̥śyantē ’ntaḥ pracurāḥ prasādā bahiś ca

children.translated_text: great warriors (<s>vārondrā</s>),
In which, endowed with many auspicious marks, plastered [edifices] are seen — inside, abundant <s>prasāda</s>s (palaces/grace), and outside,
lotus-ponds,
With splendid waves [of music/water] are viewed — inside, music halls, and outside, <s>cakroḍa</s>
side, agricultural lands,
Kept under lock by abundant grain — somehow accessed — inside, other men's wives, and out-

children.text: nānāśukavibhūṣaṇāḥ śāṁbhantē ’ntaḥ labhā vahiś ca sahakā

children.translated_text: grove kingdoms,
Adorned with various parrots [or silk garments] — are heard — inside, the [women's] chambers, and outside, the mango
reservoirs,
With the spread of fragrant substances — shine — inside, the marketplaces, and outside, the water
Why say more —
The grounds, both outside and inside, adorned with various gardens,
always bring delight to those of varied ages,

children.text: yasyāṁ ca bhaktabhājō dēvatāyatanēṣu dēvatāḥ saṁvidhānā dr̥śyantē haṭṭēṣu vaṇi

children.translated_text: folk [are seen],
In which, in the temples of the gods, the deities are seen as recipients of devotion, arranged properly; in the markets, the merchant
the gamblers,
Attentive to every syllable, in the gatherings of poets, poets are seen; in the gambling halls,

children.text: kāntārāgapriyāḥ kariṇō rājadvāraṁṣu saṁcarrānta vēśyāṅgaṇēṣu bhu

children.translated_text: men,
Elephants, fond of forest-passion, [are seen] at the royal gates; in the quarters of courtesans, the wandering
[in that most excellent city],

In which, in that [city] which is the crest-jewel of the entire circle of the earth adorned by the shores of the four oceans, with its beautiful mansions constructed of gems, putting to shame the city of <s>Indra</s>,
preverbs (<s>upasarga</s>), not in the wealth of the rich,
The unchanging state (<s>avyayabhāva</s>) [is found] in grammatical
not in the homes of the generous,
The splitting of gifts (<s>dānavicchitti</s>) [is found] on the temples of intoxicated elephants,
The cessation of enjoyment [is found only] in serpents, not among the pleasure-loving people,
incessantly-ceasing lamps of those who have ceased [burning], not in the hearts of those who have pledged [friendship].
The diminishing of affection [is found only] in the

children.text: nagarī na garīyasyā saṁpadā sā vivarjitā
vaḥ strōjanasya, vasiṣṭha iva viśvāmistratrāsajananaḥ, janamējaya iva parīkṣita
nayaḥ, paraśurāma iva paraśubhāsitaḥ, rāghava ivālaghukōdarā ḍabhaṅgarañjitajanakaḥ,
sumērur iva jātarūpasaṁpattiḥ, tuhinā cala iva puṇyabhāgīrathīsahitaḥ, cintāma
ādarśō darśanānām ācāraḥ śauryaśālinām upadēśakaḥ śastraśāstrasya, pari
vr̥ḍhō gaḍhaṁprahāriṇām, agragaṇyaḥ puṇyakāriṇām, apaścimō vipaścitām, a
nāmabhyarthayamānā iva bhagavatō viśvasr̥jaḥ kamalasaṁbhavasya karṇalagnāḥ svarga
yasmiṁś ca rājani janitajanānandē nandayati mēdinīm, gītēṣu jātisaṁ
karāḥ, tālēṣu nānālayabhaṅgāḥ, nr̥tyēṣu viṣamakaraṇaprayōgāḥ, vādyēṣu daṇḍaka
raprahārāḥ puṇyakarmārambhēṣu pravandhāḥ, sāridyūtēṣu pāśaprayōgāḥ, puṣpitakēta
kīṣu hastacchēdāḥ, nyagrōdhēṣu pādakalpanāḥ, kañcukamaṇḍanēṣu nētravikartanāni,
yaś ca kō ’py anyādr̥śa ēva lōkapālaḥ.
adaṇḍa karō dharmarājaḥ, ajaghanyaḥ pracētāḥ anuttarō dhanadaḥ.
sāninīmānaluṇṭākalōcanēna pr̥thvī priyā ca kāmarūpadhāriṇī sā tēna
gīyakāntayaḥ kuntalāḥ, ślāghanīyō nāsikyabhāgaḥ, bahulavalōkaḥ sarōmā

Victorious is <s>Hari</s>, of matchless valor, who puts an end to the sorrow of all the worlds,
whose beautiful discus-weapon flashes brilliant as a thousand suns,
who rides upon the king of birds (<s>Garuḍa</s>), who uproots the bulb of impurity,
the architect of the mansion of all the worlds!
Victorious is <s>Hari</s>, the wish-fulfilling tree for the people devoted to pure contemplation,
the crest-jewel of the host of gods who march before the city of <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>),

Moreover —
